initial_verdict: Focused repair required before acceptance of the closed-parametric contract. Core disk extremal and harmonic annulus constructions check out; exact family geometry and boundary argument ordering need correction.

required_repairs.detail: Kernel convergence plus the stated uniform small-diameter inside connectivity does not exclude a remote bubble joined by a narrowing neck. A disk can be the kernel while closed domains retain that bubble, invalidating closed inverse convergence. Restrict to the actual A_n(D_u_n) family and establish Hausdorff convergence of closed domains explicitly from convergent maps and inverses.

Individual properness of each disk map does not imply |phi_n(z_n)|->1 for varying n and boundary-approaching z_n. Prove interior map/inverse convergence first, using the actual closed-family geometry; inverse convergence on compact subdisks then gives this uniform boundary properness by contradiction.

Homeo+(R2,0) is not asserted locally compact. Use a convergent parameter sequence plus its limit, a compact parameter set, throughout common-modulus and collar estimates; sequential continuity suffices for the stated metrizable topology.

Replace the ambiguous separation paragraph by an explicit Jordan quadrilateral from two distinct Re q level rays, a trimmed small inside joining path, and a connector in a punctured pole disk outside B_R(P). For almost every intermediate radius, a component of the circle intersection joins the two level sides by the planar rectangle crossing lemma, giving the requisite fixed oscillation. Rays must follow their actual banks toward infinity.

independently_checked: The bounded-domain square-root omitted-disk construction yields an injective disk map. CC supplies extremal approximants. The normal-family maximum and square-root derivative improvement B(1+|a|)/(2sqrt|a|) give the normalized disk bijection without arbitrary-domain choice.

The Joukowski slit map is injective on the punctured disk; its pole normalization is correct. Uniform upper bounds away from the pole follow from the inverse disk-map Cauchy bound. Injectivity identifies its Dirichlet energy with bounded image area.

With the corrected circle-crosscut geometry, the angular Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and radial integration give the stated a²log(R/s) contradiction. Bank distinction recovers phi; the analogous inverse finite-area argument forbids identifying two Jordan boundary points.

The actual homeomorphism family supplies positive common inner radius, bounded outer radius, Hausdorff/kernel convergence, and small-diameter inside paths by pulling back to convex disks. Polygonal approximation of compact inside paths is legitimate.

Perron envelopes, finite maxima, local Poisson replacements, Harnack convergence and analytic-boundary barriers construct the unique harmonic measure using sequences only. Reflection across the analytic collars gives finite energy and valid normal derivatives.

The flux integral P is positive and equals energy by Green. The harmonic conjugate has periods in P Z, so the exponential is single-valued. Boundary winding and argument principle give degree-one holomorphic uniformization without assuming absence of critical points; Hopf comparison gives closed boundary homeomorphisms.

Harmonic-measure convergence, fixed-core flux convergence, reflected bounded maps and Cauchy estimates yield closed-annulus map convergence once the disk-boundary step is repaired. Compactness and injectivity then give closed inverse convergence.

All selections are finite or countable: extremal/Perron approximants, deterministic rational diagonal extraction, and finite covers of a convergent sequence together with its limit. Uniqueness defines parameter-indexed maps. No dependent-choice step or arbitrary-index choice has been identified.
